 Welcome to the Devastation Evoker rotation guide for ! This guide will teach you all about the optimal rotation for Devastation Evoker across its various talent builds. It will cover both core ability cadence and cooldown usage in dungeons and raids for .

Devastation Evoker Rotation in 

Devastation Evoker is a fairly simple and straightforward with its spell priority. Cooldowns are mostly used on cooldown, while building and spending Essence / Essence Burst .

 
 

 
 Build and Spend: Disintegrate and Pyre spend Essence , primary resource for Evokers. Living Flame and Azure Strike are the filler spells that generate Essence Burst , a proc that allows you to use these abilities without spending Essence. Spend Essence and Essence Burst, then use filler spells while waiting.
 
 

 

 
 

 
 Use cooldowns frequently: Dragonrage and Deep Breath (Scalecommander) are Devastation's main cooldown. Essence Burst is guaranteed from filler spells during this buff. Its duration can be extended by both Eternity Surge and Fire Breath with Animosity . Given that both spells also come with their own short cooldowns, consider what is available when entering Dragonrage and to press them on cooldown during it. 
 
 

 

 
 

 
 Always be casting: Try to maintain high uptime on targets. Constant use of damaging spells is the key to high damage in Raid and Mythic+. Use Hover effectively to cast spells on the move. Try to fill "downtime" in your rotation with spells, even if its not completely optimal (Azure Strike for instance). Using something is almost always better than being idle. Try to use cooldowns and Empowered spells early and often. 
 

 

Devastation Evoker Starter Guide

 Best Devastation Evoker Rotation

Hero talents also add some flavor to the rotation. Scalecommander uses Deep Breath and monitors Fire Breath duration. Aside from this, they mostly play the same.

Below, we break down the main priority lists for Devastation Evoker: Single-Target Rotation, AoE Rotation, and your opener sequence.

 Devastation in Single Target plays around a simple priority list. This means with each cast and GCD we go top to bottom on a list, and press the button with the current highest value.

 Further Details 

 Scalecommander frequently uses Deep Breath even in Single Target. In addition, each time you use Fire Breath and Eternity Surge , you gain a buff that changes Disintegrate into Mass Disintegrate .

 Hover can be cast while casting, and allows you to cast while moving. With Slipstream , a Hover charge resets with each Deep Breath . The Hover buff grows in duration with each cast, so be sure to spend a Hover charge before each Slipstream .

 Deep Breath is very strong and should be used on cooldown, but you don't want to stay in the animation longer than needed. Use the Deep Breath cancel macro found on the macros page. Here's an example of the macro for Disintegrate :
#showtooltip Disintegrate
/cancelaura Deep Breath
/cast Disintegrate

This macro will end your Deep Breath with the first press and use Disintegrate with the second. You would tap it twice, right as you hit your target.

For dots with pandemic behavior, if the dot has 30% or less of the duration of the refreshing spell, the new duration will be increased without any waste.
 

 
 Best Devastation Evoker AoE Rotation

For Devastation, AoE is defined as 3 or more targets . Devastation plays mostly the same in AoE, aside from sometimes casting Pyre . Ranking Empowered spells up can also be beneficial.

Currently, it is not worth it to rank Empowers up in Single Target or AoE. Use Fire Breath and Eternity Surge at Rank 1, unless you have Mass Disintegrate .

 Charged Blast stacks are worth tracking. Try to avoid casting Pyre in the 5 or so seconds before Dragonrage to gain 3x value on the Dragonrage Pyre s.

Pre-Combat Check

 Before any combat happens, it is important for Devastation Evoker to make sure the following are done. This applies to raids, dungeons, delves, or even open-world content.

 Devastation Evoker Major Cooldowns

Devastation Evoker has one main cooldown: Dragonrage . Other cooldowns are minor, or group buffs. The below section covers how they work, and most importantly, how to get the most out of each use.

 
 Dragonrage 

 Dragonrage is your main cooldown as Devastation. This buff guarantees Essence Burst procs from Living Flame and Azure Strike for the duration. Try to use it every 2 minutes.

Other key takeaways are:
 
Activating this spell fires 3 Pyre s at random targets.

Gain the full effect of Mastery: Giantkiller with Tyranny .

 Fire Breath and Eternity Surge extend the buff with Animosity .

 Dragonrage can be held for AoE, but it is a fairly long buff. The average duration should be around 32 seconds with proper play.

Apex talents buff your damage during this cooldown ( Rising Fury / Rising Fury )
Gain a damage buff after Dragonrage expires with Rising Fury .
 

 
 Empower Spells

 Fire Breath and Eternity Surge are Devastation's Empower spells. These can be ranked up for different effects.

Empowering Fire Breath moves damage from the debuff it applies into the initial hit of upfront damage. Leaping Flames also increases in target count per Empower level. The DoT component from Fire Breath scales dynamically with Mastery: Giantkiller , which means that the damage goes down as the target loses health. 

Empowering Eternity Surge increases the target count, and has an affect on damage talents like Shattering Stars . Eternity's Span doubles the target count per level. 

For , Fire Breath and Eternity Surge (without Tip the Scales ) should generally be used at rank 1 in Single Target and AoE.
 

 Fire Breath has two charges.

 Consume Flame uses Fire Breath to fuel explosions. This chips away at remaining duration.
 

For , Fire Breath (without Tip the Scales ) and Eternity Surge should generally be used at rank 1 in Single Target and AoE.
 

Each use of Empowered spells will enable Mass Disintegrate .

 Mass Disintegrate marks the target for Bombardments . This enables a damage proc for you and allies.
 

 
 Tip The Scales

 Tip the Scales is a minor cooldown. It is used in Dragonrage to instantly cast Eternity Surge or Fire Breath at max rank. 

For , Tip the Scales should only be used on Eternity Surge . Higher Fire Breath uptime is better for Scorching Embers , Burnout procs, Fire Breath damage via Catalyze , and Consume Flame .

For , Tip the Scales can be used on either Eternity Surge or Fire Breath . 

 
Deep Breath

 Deep Breath is another notable cooldown. This spell always gets full Mastery: Giantkiller value with Tyranny . Optimal usage depends on your Hero Talents, but it can also be used for movement or to avoid/break crowd control (stuns and roots). Always use Deep Breath at minimum range unless you need it for movement. It is important to remember that while flying, effects on the ground will still hit you, and you will be locked into the animation. Some class talents modify this ability:

 
 Imminent Destruction gives you a short buff that decreases Essence costs and increases damage.

 Strafing Run increases damage and allows for a second use.

 Onyx Legacy reduces the cooldown.

 Stretch Time takes any damage taken during the skill and stretches it out, adding some safety. 
 

 uses this spell on cooldown, due to talents like Maneuverability and Command Squadron . This version of Deep Breath can be steered, and you can eject from it.
 
Cooldown is further reduced by Bombardments procs via Wingleader .

Your Z-axis is preserved during this spell, so long as you don't fly uphill. Use height to your advantage if you plan to fly over rocky or dangerous terrain.
 
 does not typically use Deep Breath for damage, unless talents like Imminent Destruction are taken.

 
Fury of the Aspects

 Fury of the Aspects is a group cooldown, which means that when to use it is often a group decision. This spell grants you and your allies the Bloodlust effect, increasing your Haste. This spell is off the global cooldown. 

 Fury of the Aspects applies the Exhaustion debuff, locking players out of receiving similar effects for 10 minutes.

 Devastation Evoker Advanced Tips

The best thing you can do to improve your damage as a Devastation Evoker is to always be casting . Idle time in combat, caused by inactivity or poor movement, adds up and will greatly affect your damage. Mastering movement with Hover and keeping focus during combat is unequivocally the best way to raise your damage.

 
 Hover and Movement 

 Hover is your most important tool for minimizing damage losses due to movement. Hover can be cast while casting, and allows you to cast on the move. Subsequent Hover casts add to the duration, meaning you can use it again while the buff is up without wasting duration. Any time you cancel a cast because you needed to move, it created a small period of downtime. These add up and greatly reduce your damage.

 Glide is also very useful for movement, since using it is much faster than running. Simply tap your spacebar for a boost. Keep in mind, this will not work during normal casts. The trick with Glide is to triple tap, since canceling it removes the slowfall effect. This makes you travel faster, and hit the ground quicker. Bonus tip: Some ground effects can be avoided if you are at the height of your Glide .

Another interesting quirk of Hover is that it allows you to Glide while channeling Disintegrate . This is very powerful, since it allows you to quickly reposition by tapping your spacebar. Combine Hover with Glide canceling to quickly hop around the battlefield while channeling.

Not all downtime is created equal. During Dragonrage , stakes are higher. As Scalecommander, getting full value from Mass Disintegrate is also very important. For these reasons, I recommend always having a Hover in hand for cooldowns. Scalecommander has a much easier time with Hover , since each Deep Breath refunds a charge via Slipstream . Make sure you make room for this ahead of time, or the value is wasted. 

Aside from Eternity Surge and Fire Breath , all spells can be cast on the move with Hover .

 
 Deep Breath Z-axis

As Scalecommander, Deep Breath works a bit differently due to Maneuverability . One interesting property is that it preserves your Z-axis while you are flying. This can be good or bad, depending on the situation. A common situation you want to avoid is using Deep Breath uphill. Once you start scraping the ground, even a pebble can stop you in your tracks. Instead, try to gain the high ground before using Deep Breath .

Another trick is to Glide to gain altitude before Deep Breath . This helps greatly on level surfaces, since even a little added height often allows you to fly over obstacles that would normally stop you in your tracks. In some cases, added height also allows you to avoid damage ground mechanics.

 Hover and Deep Breath can also be used in tandem to cross great distances in the air. You can try this yourself: Start by jump Glide ing from a high place. Use both Hover charges to dash forward twice, then use Deep Breath until it expires. Deep Breath again, then Hover forward twice using the refunds from Slipstream . Time Spiral for one last forward Hover , then finish by reactivating Glide . In total, this is around 200 yards of movement with minimal loss of height.

 
 Disintegrate Chaining and Clipping 

 Disintegrate has 5 ticks with Azure Celerity and 4 ticks without. If channeling Disintegrate , you can cast Disintegrate again after the 4th tick without losing damage. This causes the new Disintegrate to chain in a similar "Pandemic" fashion and moves remaining duration and final tick of the previous channel to the new one. This is chaining, and you don't lose any value doing this. As a general rule, you always want to avoid downtime by chaining Disintegrate after the penultimate tick. 

As Scalecommander, avoid chaining a Mass Disintegrate into a normal Disintegrate as this will cause you to lose a percentage of the buff equal to how many ticks you clipped.

Clipping is when you cut Disintegrate short by either interrupting it with another spell or Chaining too early. Clipping is best avoided, but can be a small gain under certain circumstances. Currently, clipping non- Mass Disintegrate Disintegrate one tick early, by interrupting it for Empowers or Deep Breath , is a very small ( 0.4% ) gain for Scalecommander.

If you mess clipping up the loss will outweigh the gain, so decide for yourself if the juice is worth the squeeze.

Example Disintegrate channel (imagine this is your castbar):
 

 5 |-------------------------| 4 
 |-------------------------| 3 
 |-------------------------| 2 
 |-------------------------| 1 

 
Channels go from right to left. The first tick happens when the Disintegrate is cast. The last tick is when the channel ends.
Between 4 and 5 is ok to chain 

Let's assume you chain a second Disintegrate on the red line.
 

 5 |-------------|-----------| 4 
 |------------------------| 3 
 |------------------------| 2 
 |------------------------| 1 

 

The remainder on this last tick gets carried into the new channel. This means the new Disintegrate has 6 ticks.
 

 6 |-----------------------| 5 
 |------------------------| 4 
 |------------------------| 3 
 |------------------------| 2 
 |-------------| 1 

 

Our Devastation Evoker guides are always updated with the latest information from in-game experience, simulations, and logs. Make sure to check our changelog for this page by clicking on View Changelog in the Quick Facts column or on the book icon at the top of the page. If you are interested in more in-depth Devastation Evoker guides for , make sure to browse the Navigation Bar at the top of the page, along with our list of Related Guides just beneath the Table of Contents .

Bank 1 Fire Blast for Glorious Incandescence , but make sure to use them all before Combustion ends.
If you are above 104% haste, don't attempt to get Hot Streak! . 

Cast Fireball instead of Scorch if you already have a Hot Streak! .

This is due to extreme Haste breaking Double Pyroblast. The haste value where Scorch stop working can be lower depending on your connection to the server.

If you are already casting Fireball / Frostfire Bolt and Combustion is suddenly ready you can use that cast to enter Combustion . Scorch can also be used on the move.

Prioritize spending all Fire Blast charges in Combustion over spending all Pyroclasm . 

Stop using Fire Blast charges and Pyroclasm buffs if Combustion will be up soon to ensure they are available during cooldowns. 

If Combustion is ready, hard-cast a spell and activate Combustion right before the cast completes. Priority of spells to hard-cast:
 
 Pyroblast with Pyroclasm .

 Fireball .

 Scorch on the move.
 

If Combustion is ready, cast Meteor and activate Combustion . If Meteor isn't avialable, hard-cast a spell and activate Combustion right before the cast completes. Priority of spells to hard-cast:
 
 Pyroblast with Pyroclasm .

 Frostfire Bolt without Frostfire Empowerment .

 Scorch on the move.
 

Two simultaneous Flamestrike casts (one hard-cast, one instant with Hot Streak ) will "munch" the proc and not result in a Hot Streak . 

Hard-cast Flamestrike with Heating Up only then consume the generated Hot Streak after. 

Avoid hard-casting Flamestrike with Pyroclasm with Hot Streak already active.

The goal here is to proc Pyroclasm before the pull without entering combat.

You must activate Combustion in the last 150 milliseconds of the Pyroblast cast for this opener. 

Distance to the target is also a concern, avoid long travel times. 

 Only use this opener only if you are confident in your timing. 

 Fireball and the instant Pyroblast leave your hands at the same time. Both crit. This means you get Hot Streak for another Pyroblast . 

The purpose here to proc Essence Bomb via Essence Burst as quickly as possible.

Generally we want to avoid using Azure Strike as Flameshaper, but with extreme haste this can get us another Essence Bomb. This GCD is also a good time to Hover if needed. 

 damage on the target is greatly increased by the damage over time (DoT) effects. Ruby Embers , Enkindle , & Fire Breath must be present when you cast it for optimal gameplay.

 Ruby Embers - This DoT comes from Living Flame . You only need 1 stack on the target.

 Enkindle - This DoT comes from Essence spenders. Dragonrage casts 3 Pyre s which also apply it.

 Fire Breath - With Scorching Embers , max rank Fire Breath so long as you can while it is active. If is not ready, use at rank 1. Higher ranks do more damage but make the window smaller.

 and Iridescence also further increase the damage of .

 Charged Blast stacks to 20 and increases damage of Pyre . The exact value of stacks that makes Pyre worth casting depends.

12 stacks is the recommendation at 3 targets. 

Scalecommander gains about 0.3% damage waiting for 16 stacks at 3 targets. The difference in minimal, so 12 is the overall recommendation for the sake of simplicity.

If stacks are available for Dragonrage , they increase the damage of all 3 Pyres it casts. 

You must have enough Haste to still get 4 Empowered spells cast during Dragonrage for your extensions (via Animosity ) for this to be worth it. If your Dragonrage is less than 38 seconds on the pull, then save Eternity Surge to cast during Dragonrage .
Mastery trinkets like House of Cards (and new Season 3 ones) are the highest priority here, followed by others effects like Best-in-Slots . Other trinkets or Neural Synapse Enhancer can also be used here if you have them.
 Tip the Scales is off the Global Cooldown and can be cast ahead of time. 
Empowering this spell higher adds more targets. 

Rank 1: 1-2 Targets
Rank 2: 3-4 Targets
Rank 3: 5-6 Targets
Rank 4: 7-8 Targets ( Font of Magic )

Empowering this spell increases damage, but shortens the damage over time. 

Rank 1: During Dragonrage . 
Rank 2: Outside of Dragonrage .
Rank is flexible, and can be increased in AoE or if targets will die soon.

With Slipstream , Deep Breath resets the cooldown on Hover , avoid wasting charges by overcapping.

Hover can be used in place, and can be cast while casting.

If you are channeling Mass Disintegrate and do not have another buff, fully channel Disintegrate until the end. 

If you have two stacks of Mass Disintegrate , you can chain these casts. 

Chaining means casting another Disintegrate before the current channel ends, between the penultimate tick and the end of the channel. This transfers remaining bit of progress towards the last tick to the new channel without losing a tick.

 Mass Disintegrate will hit any valid target (in range) in front of your character. Turning your character towards additional targets in cleave will help you get more Mass Disintegrate hits.

 Disintegrate channels can be chained. 

Chaining means casting another Disintegrate before the current channel ends, between the penultimate tick and the end of the channel. This transfers remaining bit of progress towards the last tick to the new channel without losing a tick. 

Clipping means losing a tick. This can mean you interrupted your Disintegrate channel with another spell, or chained earlier than the penultimate tick. Clipping is not recommended in most cases, but we will expand on it in the Advanced section.

 Fire Breath Damage over time (DoT) should always be applied to enemies, but the duration will quickly disappear with using Essence spenders via Consume Flame . 

 Fire Breath can be reapplied to targets once the DoT is refreshable, meaning it has <= 30% duration remaining. 

Always use Fire Breath Rank 1. 

Requires Season 1 Midnight tier set ( Livery of the Black Talon ).

 
Azure Sweep damage increased by 50% and its damage against your primary target is increased by an additional 100%.

Eternity Surge grants 1 additional charge of Azure Sweep. Casting Azure Sweep reduces the cooldown of Eternity Surge by 2.0 sec.
 

 Pyre can be used to "overconsume" the Fire Breath duration via Consume Flame .

When Pyre is cast, it does not check the current Fire Breath duration for Consume Flame to deal damage. It only checks if the debuff is present.

Since Dragonrage uses 3 Pyre that all hit at the same time, it is worthwhile to shorten Fire Breath ahead of this to make use of the overconsumption. 

In Single Target, try to spend as little time in Deep Breath as possible. Cancel Deep Breath as soon as you make contact. 

Delay your second Deep Breath until Strafing Run is about to expire. Spacing these out in Single Target is worthwhile. In AOE, you can send them back to back.

 Eternity Surge and Fire Breath are roughly equal in terms of Tip the Scales value, up 4 targets.

At 5+ targets, Eternity Surge pulls ahead as the preferred option.

If Eternity Surge is not ready when Tip the Scales is up, just send it on Fire Breath .
